proposals.downside_risk: Private relays can have slower/less certain inclusion on some EVM chains, which for a latency-sensitive arbitrage cycle could reduce landed-rate and increase missed-opportunity cost; not every configured EVM chain has a mature private-relay option.

evidence.detail: Signed cycle transactions are broadcast via plain send_raw_transaction to the configured RPC with no Flashbots/private-relay or bundle submission path

Cycles are only accepted at a conservative edge after a slippage reserve; the shared strategy-lab floor elsewhere requires as little as 3-6bps net edge, a margin fully consumable by a single sandwich/frontrun

proposals.expected_effect: If frontrunning materially erodes cycle edges, routing already-qualifying cycles through a private relay (where available) could raise realized-edge-capture without any change to signal logic.
proposals.minimum_observation: At least 30 comparable opportunity pairs per chain, or 7 days of paired shadow samples, whichever is longer.
proposals.rationale: Atomic arbitrage cycles are high-value MEV targets because the entire edge is visible and copyable from the public mempool. With no private-relay/bundle path, a competing searcher can extract the discovered edge before it lands -- an EXECUTION/INFRASTRUCTURE cost that would look like 'strategy stopped working' unless measured separately from signal quality.
proposals.shadow_test: For chains with a private-relay option, run a bounded paired SHADOW comparison: for N consecutive already-passing cycle opportunities, compare public-mempool broadcast against a private-relay path (or a non-capital-committing simulation of relay inclusion odds) on landed-rate and realized-edge-vs-quoted-edge. Stop/fail condition: if relay inclusion latency exceeds the strategy's own max_signal_age_seconds threshold (e.g. 2s) in more than 20% of samples, reject the relay path as unusable for this strategy.
proposals.strategy: EVM triangular/multi-hop cycle arbitrage (route_scanner.py / market_scanner.py, executed via live_executor.py execute_cycle/execute_v3_cycle)

proposals.downside_risk: Pure accounting change with no direct trading-behavior risk; only cost is engineering effort, which is wasted if the flat-fee approximation turns out to already be immaterial.

evidence.detail: Actual execution uses a dynamic priority-fee cap and persists real network_fee_lamports/priority_fee_lamports/jito_tip_lamports per signature in live_execution_receipts

proposals.expected_effect: Reconciling strategy P&L against live_execution_receipts fee fields would tighten the accuracy of net-P&L figures gating stop-loss, canary promotion, and the platform-wide profit-factor throttle.
proposals.minimum_observation: At least 50 matched trade/receipt pairs, or 14 days of history, whichever is available first.
proposals.rationale: Strategy-level realized P&L used for stop-loss/take-profit/canary-promotion decisions appears to subtract a flat conservative fee estimate rather than the dynamic priority fee actually paid and already recorded elsewhere. During Solana priority-fee spikes this understates true cost and can overstate net edge, misclassifying EXECUTION cost as STRATEGY profit and risking premature canary promotion on an inflated number.
proposals.shadow_test: Read-only backfill: for a bounded historical sample of already-executed Solana SiMo trades, compare the flat-fee-based net P&L already recorded against a recomputed net P&L using the matching live_execution_receipts row for the same signature. No new capital or live-behavior change required. Stop condition: if the two P&L series diverge by less than a set materiality threshold (e.g. <1% of average trade size) across the sample, treat the current approximation as adequate and close the finding.
proposals.strategy: Solana SiMo copy-trading P&L accounting (solana_sibot.py) reconciled against live execution fee receipts (solana_execution_efficiency_patch.py)

proposals.downside_risk: A submission lock adds latency by serializing otherwise-parallel opportunity execution on the same wallet; a naive gas-bump could resubmit into a since-unprofitable trade if not re-validated first.

evidence.detail: get_transaction_count(address, 'pending') fetched fresh per call with no lock/mutex guarding the fetch-then-sign-then-send sequence across concurrent triggers

No gas-bump/replace-by-fee/'speed up' logic found; a stuck pending transaction times out (wait_for_transaction_receipt(timeout=120)) into a manual-intervention error rather than being resubmitted at higher gas

proposals.expected_effect: A per-wallet-per-chain submission lock plus an optional fee-bump-and-resubmit path (re-validated against the existing profit gate before bumping) would reduce infra-caused execution failures without touching strategy signal logic.
proposals.minimum_observation: 30 days of existing execution logs (no new shadow run needed to first confirm the collision occurs in practice).
proposals.rationale: Multiple independent live-trading entry points exist per EVM wallet (AUTO scanner, SiMo copy engine, manual commands). Without a serialization lock, near-simultaneous nonce fetches can collide, producing a dropped/stuck transaction that surfaces as a failed execution rather than a bad strategy signal; with no gas-bump path, a transaction stuck under a rising base fee simply times out instead of completing, under-executing otherwise-profitable opportunities in a way that would misleadingly look like poor strategy performance unless separated out.
proposals.shadow_test: This is a code-correctness/execution-quality question rather than a P&L hypothesis -- validate first via a runtime audit of existing execution logs (e.g. execution_latency.py samples) for wallets/chains with multiple submissions in the same block window and their nonce-error rate versus baseline, before any code change. Stop condition: if collision-linked failures are near zero in the observed log window, close as non-issue without code change.
proposals.strategy: EVM live execution transaction submission serialization (live_executor.py), shared across AUTO arbitrage scanner, SiMo copy engine, and manual commands

proposals.downside_risk: Retrospective log-tagging has no trading-behavior risk; it is pure reporting overhead if repeated halt-style incidents don't recur.

evidence.detail: One-shot platform-wide Solana LIVE kill switch dated 2026-08-18 citing 'repeated Solana loss/exit-retry pattern' without separating strategy loss from execution/liquidity-gate-blocked exits

Loss-driven stop-loss exits route through the same liquidity/impact gates as normal exits (with only a wider emergency ceiling), so a stop-loss can itself be delayed or blocked by the liquidity gate rather than executing at the intended trigger level

proposals.expected_effect: Logging each stop-loss-triggered exit as 'executed at trigger', 'executed via emergency-unwind wider ceiling', or 'still liquidity-blocked/escalated' would let a future incident review correctly separate bad entries/signals from exits unable to clear liquidity gates at the desired size/time.
proposals.minimum_observation: The full set of positions closed or halted in the 2026-08-18 incident, if retrievable; otherwise this becomes a forward-looking logging improvement for the next incident.
proposals.rationale: A recent platform-wide halt explicitly conflated 'loss' with 'exit-retry pattern' in its own migration comment. If stop-losses were being delayed/blocked by the liquidity gate rather than price movement being the primary driver, the realized loss and the halt decision are actually an EXECUTION/INFRASTRUCTURE finding, not evidence the strategy's edge went negative -- these require different fixes and the current incident record does not distinguish them.
proposals.shadow_test: Read-only forensic reconstruction, not a capital-risking test: for the positions implicated in the 2026-08-18 halt (if still queryable), classify each loss-driving exit as price-driven-at-trigger vs liquidity-gate-delayed/escalated and report the split. Stop condition: if the underlying data can no longer be reconstructed, mark as an evidence gap rather than guessing.
proposals.strategy: Solana stop-loss / emergency-exit root-cause attribution (solana_sibot.py stop-loss, solana_emergency_liquidity_unwind_patch.py, solana_emergency_loss_halt_migration.py)

proposals.downside_risk: An overly sensitive counter could pause EVM live trading on transient/unrelated RPC blips; Solana's default (2 faults) is aggressive and would need chain-appropriate tuning given EVM's existing route/token quarantine already absorbs some of this.

evidence.detail: Solana auto-disables solana_live_enabled after live_no_output_disable_after (default 2) consecutive landed-but-invalid execution faults
EVM only has route/token-scoped quarantine (300s route, 21600s token after 3 strikes), with no equivalent wallet/account-level auto-disable after repeated execution-mismatch faults

proposals.expected_effect: Adding an EVM-side execution-fault counter mirroring the existing Solana pattern would close a chain-asymmetric gap without touching any strategy signal or sizing logic.
proposals.minimum_observation: 30 days of EVM live execution logs monitored in read-only/shadow mode before considering an actual auto-disable wire-up.
proposals.rationale: Solana has a dedicated per-user auto-disable safety net for ambiguous/invalid execution outcomes, distinct from strategy loss; no equivalent was found for EVM. This is a chain-symmetry gap in the execution/infra safety net: repeated EVM execution-mismatch faults (e.g. from an RPC provider issue or a router/ABI change) would only quarantine the specific route/token, not pause the account's EVM live trading the way Solana does.
proposals.shadow_test: Not capital-risking: implement first as a read-only monitoring counter (log what the auto-disable would have triggered had it existed) over a bounded observation window, before wiring it to actually disable EVM live trading. Stop condition: if zero or near-zero qualifying faults are observed over the window, deprioritize as low-value for current EVM reliability.
proposals.strategy: EVM live-trading execution-fault circuit breaker (no account-level auto-disable equivalent to Solana's solana_execution_fault_counter_patch.py)

summary: Architecture-only review (no fresh runtime forensics). The bot runs three parallel strategy families -- EVM triangular/multi-hop arbitrage (route_scanner.py/market_scanner.py/live_executor.py), directional leader-copy trading on both chains (sibot.py/solana_sibot.py), and a governed, non-signing market-native Strategy Lab (cross_chain_strategy_signals.py/shadow_strategy_executor.py/strategy_canary.py) -- all sharing multi-layer pre-trade profitability, slippage, price-impact, liquidity and sellability gates. The safety architecture (execution quarantine, exit circuit breakers, platform profit-factor throttle, AI-council + staged canary promotion) is comparatively mature. The main gaps found are EXECUTION/INFRASTRUCTURE rather than strategy-signal issues: EVM arbitrage cycles broadcast via public mempool with no MEV/private-relay protection despite razor-thin (3-6bps) required edges; Solana strategy-level P&L bookkeeping uses a flat fee estimate that may diverge from the dynamic priority fee actually paid and recorded elsewhere; EVM has no nonce-submission lock or gas-bump/RBF path and no wallet-level execution-fault kill switch analogous to Solana's; and a recent platform-wide Solana loss halt (2026-08-18) conflated realized loss with exit-retry/liquidity-gate behavior in its own commit message, which is exactly the strategy-vs-execution conflation this review is asked to avoid. No claim of measured live profitability or canary readiness is made given the missing runtime evidence.
